name: Switch with pilot light plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a switch with an integral pilot lamp that shows when the controlled load is on.
description: A switch with pilot light is used where the controlled load cannot be seen from the switch position, such as an external light, a water heater or a loft. The plan form adds a small lamp mark, a crossed circle, to the switch symbol.

The pilot lamp needs a neutral at the switch in many accessory designs, so the symbol tells the electrician to bring a neutral to the switch box. It may also signal a double-pole switch for appliance control.
The lamp mark does not tell you whether it lights when the load is on or when the switch is off as a locator. The specification decides.
readingNotes: Check whether the lamp indicates load on or acts as a locator.
Confirm a neutral is available at the switch.
distinction: A plain one-way switch has no lamp; this form adds visual confirmation of the load state.
